newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH UTILITY DASHES DIVIDEND HOPES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH UTILITY DASHES DIVIDEND HOPES.

text.p: Czech heating utility Prazska Teplarenska a.s. said on Monday it does not plan to pay out dividends in the next few years despite an expected increase in profits this year.
This was due to due to high investment needs, it said.
"We have to reinvest a large part of the profit. The company won't pay out (dividends) for quite a long time," Teplarenska's deputy chairman Boris Vostry told a news conference.
The firm's half-year pre-tax profit climbed to 793 million crowns in the first six months of this year from 469 million in the same period of 1995.
Company officials said this year's final net result would be better than last year's 281 million crowns, but they have declined to give a detailed forecast.
The firm supplies Prague households and industries. About 60 percent of its supplies are subject to government price regulations for households.
Teplarenska expects in its financial plan that the regulations will be completely lifted before 1999.
The company said it intends to invest over nine billion crowns over the next 15 years, mainly into co-generating units with heat produced as a by-product in electric power plants sold to households.

The company is controlled by Cyprus-based Daventree investment group of U.S. enterpreneur Michael Dingman which together with Czech partner Harvardsky Prumyslovy Holding a.s. holds 44 percent. The city of Prague holds 25 percent and Germany's GESO 21 percent of the company's stock.
